situation:
You are the assistant manager at ALDER CREEK RECREATION CENTER, a gym and community recreation center that one family has run for three generations. The owner (judge), the third of that family to hold the job, has asked you to recommend how the center should use its weekday afternoons next season.

The center leases its building from the city below market, and in return it promised to keep weekday afternoons open to town youth leagues at no charge. Those free hours are what the center is known for. They are run by one program manager, who now spends most of the week posting to the center's social media instead.

Attendance at those hours has fallen, and the account the manager posts from is a personal one that has become the center's main channel. KESTREL UNITED ATHLETIC CLUB, a regional travel club, has offered to lease the same afternoons for its teams, at a rate that would cover the center's summer payroll and would close the free hours the city lease rests on.

The owner (judge) wants you to recommend whether to take the lease or return the program manager to the youth hours and forgo that money, and to say how either choice is carried out. You will present in the owner's (judge) office. The owner (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and thank you for your work after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the owner (judge) of ALDER CREEK RECREATION CENTER, the third generation of your family to run it. Business background is the same as the situation above. The travel club wants an answer before it sets its own season, and the city lease comes up for renewal the year after.

You want the assistant manager to recommend whether to lease the weekday afternoons or return the program manager to the youth hours, and to say how that choice would actually be carried out.

During the presentation you are to ask the following questions of the participant:
judgeQuestions: What is the first step, and who takes it?
What has to be in place before the season starts?
